paragraphs.text: The Harmony of the Gospels, Book II

Chapter 58. Of the Man Who Brought Before Him His Son, Whom the Disciples Were Unable to Heal; And of the Question Concerning the Agreement Between These Three Evangelists Also in the Matter of the Order of Narration Here.

116. Matthew goes on in the following terms: <quote>And when He had come to the multitude, there came to Him a certain man, kneeling down before Him, and saying, Lord, have mercy on my son; for he is lunatic, and sore vexed;</quote> and so on, down to the words, <quote>Howbeit this kind is not cast out but by prayer and fasting.</quote> Both Mark and Luke record this incident, and that, too, in the same order, without any suspicion of a want of harmony.
